title: The Miraculousness And Testimony Of The Quran 17th Degree 3rd Point The Challenge Of Eloquence And Its Inimitability

questions.question: What happened when the desert poet heard the verse being recited?
questions.answer: He immediately fell in prostration.

questions.question: What reason did the poet give for his prostration?
questions.answer: He said he was not accepting Islam at that moment, but was bowing because of the power and beauty of the verse’s language.

questions.question: According to the passage, what did many experts in language and rhetoric agree about the Qur’an’s style?
questions.answer: They agreed that its eloquence is beyond what human beings can produce.

questions.question: How did the Qur’an challenge proud speakers and writers?
questions.answer: It called on them to produce even one chapter equal to it.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from the fact that its opponents chose conflict and sacrifice instead of meeting that challenge directly?
questions.answer: It shows they were unable to answer the challenge by producing something like it.

questions.question: How does the passage use the many Arabic books written by both supporters and enemies of the Qur’an as evidence?
questions.answer: It says that even with so many attempts to imitate it or oppose it, none reached its level.

questions.question: What judgment does the passage say even an ordinary listener would make when comparing the Qur’an with other books?
questions.answer: Such a listener would see that it is in a different and higher category.

questions.question: Why does the passage say the Qur’an cannot be considered lower than other books?
questions.answer: Because no sensible person, not even among unbelievers, could honestly claim that.

questions.question: What main idea ties together the examples of the poet, the scholars, and the failed challengers?
questions.answer: All of them point to the unmatched eloquence and unique status of the Qur’an.

questions.question: What kind of proof is emphasized most strongly in this passage: historical, scientific, or literary? Explain briefly.
questions.answer: Literary proof, because the passage mainly focuses on language, eloquence, and the inability of others to match it.

questions.question: Who are mentioned as having reached a united judgment about the Qur’an’s eloquence?
questions.answer: Scholars and masters of literature and rhetoric are mentioned.

questions.question: What does their united judgment add to the argument in the passage?
questions.answer: It strengthens the claim by showing that qualified experts agreed on it, not just a few individuals.

questions.question: In the passage, what was the response of the Bedouin poet when people thought he might have become Muslim?
questions.answer: He clarified that his prostration came from amazement at the verse’s eloquence.

questions.question: What does this reaction suggest about the effect of the Qur’an’s language on listeners?
questions.answer: It suggests that its language can deeply move even someone who has not yet embraced the faith.

questions.question: What challenge does the Qur’an present to its opponents?
questions.answer: It dares them to produce one surah comparable to it.

questions.question: Why is producing one surah described as the short path?
questions.answer: Because it would have been the easiest direct way to answer the Qur’an’s claim if they had truly been able to do so.

questions.question: What does the passage infer from their choosing danger instead of taking that short path?
questions.answer: It infers that they had no ability to meet the challenge.

questions.question: How does the passage compare the Qur’an with the large number of Arabic books in circulation?
questions.answer: It says none of those books, whether friendly or hostile to the Qur’an, reaches the same level.

questions.question: What is the significance of saying the Qur’an is either above those books or below them?
questions.answer: It sets up a clear comparison, then argues that since nobody can reasonably place it below them, it must be above them.

questions.question: What overall claim about the Qur’an is being defended in this passage?
questions.answer: The passage is defending that the Qur’an’s eloquence is unmatched and beyond human imitation.

questions.question: What did the poet from the desert do as soon as he heard the verse?
questions.answer: He prostrated right away.

questions.question: Did he say his action meant he had entered Islam? Give the fuller answer.
questions.answer: No. He said his action was a response to the extraordinary eloquence of the verse.

questions.question: Why is this story important in the passage’s argument?
questions.answer: It gives a real example of how strongly the Qur’an’s language affected a listener.

questions.question: What do the named scholars represent in the passage?
questions.answer: They represent highly respected authorities in eloquence and rhetoric.

questions.question: What was their common conclusion about the Qur’an?
questions.answer: They concluded that human beings cannot reach its level of expression.

questions.question: What did the Qur’an call proud literary people to do?
questions.answer: It called them to bring forth a chapter like it if they could.

questions.question: What warning was attached to that challenge?
questions.answer: The challenge came with the message that refusal and failure would lead to disgrace and loss.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention books written by both allies and opponents of the Qur’an?
questions.answer: To show that many people tried from different motives, yet none could equal it.

questions.question: According to the passage, how would an average person likely rank the Qur’an beside those books?
questions.answer: The average person would recognize that the Qur’an stands higher than them.

questions.question: What can we infer about the passage’s view of human literary talent compared with the Qur’an?
questions.answer: Human talent is seen as limited, while the Qur’an is presented as far beyond that limit.

questions.question: What immediate effect did one verse have on the Bedouin poet?
questions.answer: It moved him to prostrate on the spot.

questions.question: What does his explanation show about his understanding of the verse?
questions.answer: It shows he recognized an exceptional beauty and force in its wording.

questions.question: How does the passage use expert testimony after giving this individual example?
questions.answer: It moves from one personal reaction to the broad agreement of many specialists.

questions.question: What field were the mentioned experts known for?
questions.answer: They were known for language, rhetoric, and literary analysis.

questions.question: What was the Qur’an’s challenge to arrogant speakers and writers meant to do to their pride?
questions.answer: It was meant to humble them by exposing their inability to match it.

questions.question: What practical choice did the opponents make instead of answering the challenge?
questions.answer: They chose a costly path that put their lives and wealth at risk.

questions.question: Why does the passage treat that choice as evidence?
questions.answer: Because if they could have answered the challenge easily, they would not have taken the more dangerous option.

questions.question: How does the passage use comparison with other Arabic writings to support its claim?
questions.answer: It argues that all attempts to imitate or oppose the Qur’an still fall short when compared with it.

questions.question: What role does the “common man” play in the argument?
questions.answer: He shows that the difference is so clear that even a regular listener can notice it.

questions.question: State the central conclusion of the whole passage in one sentence.
questions.answer: The Qur’an’s language is presented as uniquely elevated and impossible for human beings to equal.

questions.question: In the account given, what mistaken assumption did people make about the poet’s prostration?
questions.answer: They assumed he had become Muslim.

questions.question: How did he correct that assumption?
questions.answer: He said his prostration was in response to the verse’s eloquence, not a declaration of conversion.

questions.question: What does this detail add to the force of the example?
questions.answer: It shows that even without conversion, the listener still felt overwhelmed by the verse’s power.

questions.question: What kind of agreement existed among the many scholars and literary masters mentioned?
questions.answer: They shared a unanimous view that the Qur’an’s eloquence cannot be reached by human effort.

questions.question: What invitation did the Qur’an give to its opponents in the literary arena?
questions.answer: It invited them to produce one surah like it.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying they left the short path for the long path?
questions.answer: It means they avoided the direct test of imitation and instead entered harmful struggle and resistance.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage draw from that behavior?
questions.answer: It concludes that they could not meet the challenge.

questions.question: Why are books by both friends and enemies mentioned together?
questions.answer: Because both groups had reasons to write in relation to the Qur’an, yet neither group produced anything equal to it.

questions.question: According to the passage, what would be an unreasonable claim about the Qur’an and other books?
questions.answer: It would be unreasonable to claim that the Qur’an ranks below them.

questions.question: What action of the Bedouin poet opens this passage’s argument?
questions.answer: His prostration after hearing a verse opens the argument.

questions.question: What inner response caused that action?
questions.answer: He felt deep awe at the verse’s eloquence.

questions.question: Besides this poet, what larger group also supports the passage’s view?
questions.answer: A large body of scholars and literary experts also supports it.

questions.question: What did those experts decide about the Qur’an’s eloquence?
questions.answer: They decided that it cannot be matched by human beings.

questions.question: How does the Qur’an address proud people of language and rhetoric in the passage?
questions.answer: It confronts them with a challenge to produce a single surah like it.

questions.question: What does their failure to do so suggest about their actual ability?
questions.answer: It suggests that they did not have the power to match it.

questions.question: How do the many Arabic books mentioned function as comparative evidence?
questions.answer: They serve as examples showing that repeated attempts across time still did not reach the Qur’an’s level.

questions.question: What observation is attributed to an ordinary listener comparing the Qur’an with those books?
questions.answer: The listener would recognize that the Qur’an is not in the same class as the others.

questions.question: If it cannot reasonably be placed beneath the other books, what conclusion follows?
questions.answer: The conclusion is that it stands above them.
